extracted.intended_audience: Postdoctoral researchers applying for HFSP Long‑Term (LTF) or Cross‑Disciplinary (CDF) Fellowships (Award Year 2027)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory criteria for preparing and submitting HFSP Long‑Term and Cross‑Disciplinary postdoctoral fellowship applications for Award Year 2027, including eligibility, required documents (LOI and Full Proposal), publication requirements, host/host‑supervisor rules, financial/contractual conditions, ethical/data/IP rules, and reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program mission, objectives, and features
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP aims to strengthen open scientific enquiry by supporting international, interdisciplinary, collaborative, and cutting‑edge basic research in the life sciences. Fellows are expected to incorporate novel investigative approaches at the frontiers of the life sciences, disrupt existing paradigms, move to a new country/institution, and broaden their expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP funds exploratory research without the need for preliminary data, offers three years (36 months) of funding including living and research & travel allowances, and expects fellows to pursue projects significantly different from their prior work and to develop interdisciplinary collaborations and new career directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of fellowship: LTF vs CDF
rubrics_metrics.description: Two categories: Long‑Term Fellowships (LTF) for applicants with prior life‑sciences training/experience; Cross‑Disciplinary Fellowships (CDF) for applicants with non‑life‑sciences PhDs and little/no prior biology experience. Both require the proposed project to be in the life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Table 1 to decide which fellowship to apply for. CDF applicants must bring a unique non‑life‑science skill set to a fundamental biological problem; LTF applicants must show how the project differs from their previous life‑science work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful LTF proposal characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful LTF proposals: incorporate novel investigative approaches at the frontiers of the life sciences; show clearly how the project differs from the applicant’s prior research; demonstrate ability to formulate frontier‑extending, risky projects; describe how applicant’s unique training will allow novel approaches; anticipate impact beyond immediate topic; generate new research directions for the host lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize novelty, difference from prior work, risk/disciplinary frontiers, applicant's unique contribution, and broader impact when drafting an LTF proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful CDF proposal characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful CDF proposals: incorporate novel investigative approaches with potential to disrupt paradigms; demonstrate the applicant’s change of field and how their non‑life‑science training will address a fundamental biological problem in a novel way; clearly explain difference from applicant’s prior work; formulate frontier‑extending, risky projects; combine life and non‑life sciences to generate new directions for applicant and host lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight the applicant’s transferrable skills, the novelty arising from cross‑disciplinary combination, and training/learning outcomes in the life sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific scope: basic life‑science research required
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research must be basic, fundamental research within the life sciences (examples: genes, molecules, biophysics, intracellular networks, tissues/organs, organismal functions including cognitive functions, populations and ecosystems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project must be distinctly different from the applicant’s PhD/previous postdoc work and primarily the applicant’s idea (host consultation allowed). HFSP supports exploratory basic research; applicants uncertain of fit may contact fellow@hfsp.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research topics not supported
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP does not fund: projects of a purely applied nature (e.g., primarily clinical/pharmaceutical, drug design/development, applied engineering/biotech/nanotech, development of novel methods that do not aim to answer a basic biological question, projects directly focused on agricultural/forestry/environmental/conservational problems); purely observational/descriptive projects (including systematic screening and data collection studies); proposals that are an obvious next step in the field using standard approaches or only promise incremental advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also not funded: projects that are an obvious next step in the host lab or a close continuation of the applicant’s prior PhD/postdoc work, and research in for‑profit environments (collaborations allowed). Frame proposals as basic, novel, and frontier‑extending.

rubrics_metrics.name: One application per year and change requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In one year, each applicant may submit only one Letter of Intent (for either LTF or CDF) and must propose a change in country AND a change in research topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsuccessful applicants may reapply in subsequent years if still eligible. Ensure your proposed host and project meet the change requirements before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host supervisor endorsement limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each host supervisor may only endorse ONE applicant (LOI) per competition year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm with your proposed host supervisor that they have not and will not endorse another HFSP Fellowship application in the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship may only be held once
rubrics_metrics.description: An HFSP postdoctoral fellowship may only be held once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who have previously held an HFSP postdoctoral fellowship are ineligible to hold another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation date window
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applicants must begin (activate) their fellowship between 1 April 2027 and 1 January 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan host lab arrival and administrative steps to ensure activation within this window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and host country eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationality rules: nationals of HFSPO Member Countries can apply to work in any country of which they are NOT a national; candidates not nationals of HFSPO Member Countries can only apply to work in an HFSPO Member Country. Dual nationals may apply to work in one of their countries of nationality only if they have never lived in that country and meet the other nationality criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all cases, host country/institution criteria must also be satisfied. Contact fellow@hfsp.org for clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host country and host institution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must: propose a change in country; propose a research institution in a host country they are not a national of; not propose to take up the fellowship in the country where they obtained their PhD; not have studied or worked in the proposed host country for more than 12 months (total) by the activation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international/extraterritorial institutions (e.g., EMBL), the country where the lab is located is considered the host country. For‑profit research environments are not eligible host institutions (collaborations allowed). Applicants already at the proposed host are eligible ONLY if they arrived on/after 1 April 2026 and must activate within 12 months of arrival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host supervisor relationship restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot propose host supervisors who are former scientific collaborators, former research supervisors, or with whom they have worked or published. Applications are ineligible if the applicant has spent more than 12 months (total) working with the proposed host supervisor by the activation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposed host supervisor can endorse only one LOI per year. If two host supervisors are proposed, both must provide their information and letters at the Full Proposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral degree timing and conferral window
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have completed their PhD (or equivalent) before starting the fellowship and before 31 December 2027. Applicants are ineligible if the doctoral degree was conferred more than 3 years (36 months) prior to the Full Proposal submission deadline (i.e., conferral prior to 24 September 2023 is ineligible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some post‑PhD career interruptions (illness, parental leave, full‑time caregiving, military/civil service) may be exempted if documented BEFORE initiating LOI; other interruptions (unemployment, internships, paid/unpaid employment) are not eligible for exemption. Enter interruption dates in the CV section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead‑author publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have at least one full‑length original research publication in English for which the applicant is a lead author (single author, first author, or joint‑first author). Review articles and patents do not qualify for this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At LOI stage the lead author manuscript must be (i) published, (ii) accepted/in press, (iii) accepted for publication, or (iv) available in a recognized OA preprint repository AND submitted to a peer‑reviewed journal. At Full Proposal stage option (iv) is NO LONGER valid — the lead author manuscript must be published, accepted/in‑press, or accepted for publication. If first authorship conventions differ (alphabetical authorship), explain in Additional Comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI initiation and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible, applicants must initiate their Letter of Intent in ProposalCentral by opening and saving the online form to obtain a 7‑digit LOI ID by 5 May 2026, and submit the completed LOI by 12 May 2026 (both by 09:00 Eastern US Time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ProposalCentral opens 12 March 2026. Ensure timely initiation to obtain LOI ID. The LOI should succinctly summarize the planned project (see LOI content requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI required content
rubrics_metrics.description: LOI must include: project title; personal info (name, ORCID, email, degrees, short CV); proposed host institution/supervisor(s) and intended arrival date; disclosure of previous/current collaborations with host; title and abstract of PhD thesis and prior postdoc projects; summary of proposed research (background, aims, central hypotheses, experimental approach, expected outcomes) up to 3000 characters; THREE key references; publication list and additional info on publications; confirmation that host supervisor(s) are aware and support the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No host signatures or further host documents are required at LOI stage. Use the ProposalCentral templates (e.g., for publication list). Do not have the host supervisor endorse more than one LOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Proposal required content and character limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Proposal (invited applicants only) must include: recommendation letter(s) from host supervisor(s); two additional referees' reference letters; contact info for host institution official and host supervisor(s); detailed research plan including summary (carried over), background & significance (up to 3000 characters), specific aims (up to 8000 characters), experimental design (up to 6000 characters), bibliography (up to 15 refs), how project differs from applicant’s previous work (up to 2500 characters), why project is leading edge (up to 4000 characters), why host lab is a good fit (up to 2000 characters); a public summary (up to 2400 characters); publication list and additional publication info; signatures of applicant, host supervisor(s), and host institution official (electronic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character counts include spaces and punctuation. Host supervisor(s) and referees must submit/complete their sections and sign before applicant can submit. The proposal can be modified after signatures are collected, but cannot be submitted until all signatures are registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host supervisor recommendation letter contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In the host supervisor template, they must: register a brief list of career and research experience; include up to 10 relevant publications; explain how the applicant’s proposed research is a new direction for their lab and how it is a significant change from the applicant’s prior work; explain how/why their lab is suited to supporting HFSP aims; and outline a mentorship plan for the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two host supervisors are listed, BOTH must provide their information and letters. Host supervisor sections must be submitted before the applicant can submit the Full Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter requirements (external referees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two additional referees must provide reference letters at the Full Proposal stage, describing their impression of the applicant in no more than 3000 characters (including spaces) using the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter referee contact info in ProposalCentral so they receive email directions and templates; ensure referees know the character limit and prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: All LOIs are assessed for eligibility and by Review Committee members; highest scoring LOIs are invited to submit Full Proposals. Full Proposals are assessed by external scientific reviewers and then by Review Committee members; proposals are discussed and ranked at the Review Committee meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criteria and a scoring guide for reviewers are available separately. The application and selection processes are confidential; reviewers should evaluate proposals on their scientific content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications evaluation and DORA policy
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP is a signatory to DORA: reviewers evaluate research proposals on the basis of content, not Journal Impact Factors (JIF). Reviewers should consider the quality and influence of candidates’ publications (including preprints) in advancing knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP reviewers are asked to consider influence and content over JIF; consult HFSP policy regarding preprint servers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures and submission blocking rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Full Proposal cannot be submitted until host supervisor(s), referees (their sections), and the host institution official have submitted their sections and the required electronic signatures have been registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ahead to obtain host and institutional signatures; proposals can be modified after signatures are collected but not submitted until all signatures present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of award: duration, FTE, and activation
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP Fellowship is awarded for 3 years (36 months), cannot be renewed, and fellows must begin between 1 April 2027 and 1 January 2028. Fellowship allowances are administered through the host institution and the appointment must be 100% FTE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows should investigate tax liabilities and visa requirements; ensure host institution accepts HFSP rules for externally funded postdocs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living allowance payment and deduction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution agrees to pay the fellow the full living allowance (which may not represent the fellow’s full salary). Legally compulsory deductions (taxation, social security, health insurance, pension contributions) may be made if required by law, but no other deductions (institutional overheads, bench fees) are allowed. HFSPO does not provide additional funds for health insurance/pension/other benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions may top up the living allowance to meet local salary requirements; applicants should check whether top‑ups are possible and expected salary levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & travel allowance, relocation and child allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP awards a research & travel allowance (for reagents, equipment, conference travel) and may provide a relocation allowance. Fellows with children receive a child allowance set at 10% of the applicable Year‑1 living allowance. Fellows may apply for up to 3 months paid parental leave for children born/adopted during the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowances are listed in Appendix tables but are under review and may change before final offer. Relocation allowance schedules and additional allowances for spouse/children are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent fellowships/grants and employment restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP Fellows cannot concurrently hold an HFSP Fellowship and another paid employment position or another paid fellowship. The HFSP living allowance can be supplemented from other sources but must not be used as the fellow’s salary. Fellows may apply for additional research grants to assist the conduct of the fellowship research but those funds must not be used as fellows’ salary. Fellows must devote themselves entirely to their HFSP research and may not engage in any other paid activity without prior HFSPO agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify with HFSPO and host if considering salary supplements, additional grants, or paid activities; obtain prior agreement if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may interrupt ('defer') HFSPO support for up to two years (24 months) after completing at least one year of the HFSP Fellowship, to spend up to two years in a different laboratory (at same or different institution) or to conduct research in a new country. All deferrals require prior approval by HFSPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit deferral requests with justification and obtain HFSPO approval before interrupting the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑year flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In the third year fellows may choose to remain in the host laboratory, return to their or their spouse’s/partner’s home country, or move to another HFSPO member country; moves require prior HFSP approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan third‑year arrangements and seek HFSP approval for moves as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical standards and misconduct reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must observe the highest ethical standards and conform to national and institutional codes, regulations and laws governing ethical conduct of research. Institutions must inform HFSPO if national or institutional codes have been infringed during award performance. Fellows must agree not to undertake research jointly with scientists in another country where experimental procedures forbidden in their own institutions are permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with institutional/national ethical rules and HFSPO Policy on Scientific Misconduct; include ethics considerations in proposal if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of private/sensitive personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed project involves collection/processing of sensitive personal data (health, sexual lifestyle, ethnicity, political opinion, religion, genetic information, etc.) or genetic data, applicants must justify the need, discuss ethical implications and how they will be addressed in the appropriate proposal section. For observational work involving participants, state whether videos/photos will be used publicly and describe privacy/informed consent measures; for existing data, specify sources and authorization for secondary use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe consent, privacy guarantees, and data authorization; contact HFSPO for questions on data use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of personal data (GDPR and privacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO is committed to safeguarding applicants’ personal information in accordance with GDPR (EU) 2016/679 and transfers of personal data outside EU/EEA. The HFSPO Privacy Policy explains how personal information is collected, stored and used for applicants and successful candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the HFSPO Privacy Policy to understand data handling and applicant rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property rights and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSPO will not claim intellectual or commercial property rights arising from sponsored research and will not become involved in disputes on ownership. Assignment of rights and income is determined by host laboratory/institution procedures. Submission of manuscripts for publication shall not be delayed for more than 45 working days after the manuscript is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge HFSP support (with fellowship number/DOI) in all publications. Consult host institution policies for IP assignment. HFSP is engaged in research security discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and open access policy
rubrics_metrics.description: An acknowledgement with fellowship number/DOI of HFSP support must be included in all publications resulting from fellowship work. HFSPO open‑access policy is available at hfsp.org/Open‑Access‑Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow HFSP open‑access guidance and include required acknowledgement in manuscripts, preprints, and presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in application writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI and AI‑assisted technologies may only be used to improve readability and language of the application, not to create content. Applicants must disclose their use of AI/AI‑assisted technologies in the application. HFSPO may check AI use with software and take outcomes into account in evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid entering confidential project details into external AI services. HFSP does not encourage using AI to determine eligibility/alignment of proposed research because tools may be outdated and criteria may change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances are subject to change (appendix tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP provides country‑specific yearly living allowances, child allowances, research & travel allowances, and relocation allowances as listed in the Appendix tables; these allowances are currently under review and may be subject to change before final offers are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact fellow@hfsp.org for details of countries not listed or for updated allowance information; do not assume appendix figures are final until offer.
